hero.headline: Audio and text accommodation for provincial assessments.
hero.subtitle: A Chrome extension and teacher dashboard that delivers audio and text support for assessed students on managed Chromebooks, without storing any student data.

howItWorks.label: How it works
howItWorks.headline: Three steps. No IT ticket required.
howItWorks.step1Body: Sign in with your school Google account, upload an audio file or paste assessment text, and get a short access code and exit word. Takes under a minute.
howItWorks.step2Body: The student types the access code into the AudioProctor extension on their Chromebook. A locked fullscreen player opens for audio, or a read-aloud text reader for text assessments.
howItWorks.step3Body: When the assessment is done, the teacher reads the exit word aloud. The student types it in, the player closes, and the Chromebook returns to normal.

why.label: Why AudioProctor
why.headline: Designed around a real gap in how assessments work.
why.col1Body: Students are anonymous to the system. No names, no student IDs, no device identifiers. This isn't just a policy. It's structural. There's no place in the database to store student information.
why.col2Title: Deployed by IT, not installed by teachers
why.col2Body: The Chrome extension is force-installed via Google Admin Console. Every Chromebook in the division gets it automatically. Teachers never touch a settings page.
why.col3Title: Built for how assessments actually work
why.col3Body: Supports both audio and text-based accommodations in a single tool. The access code model, the lockdown player, and the exit word were all designed around the real friction of delivering accommodations in the classroom.

useCases.label: Use Cases
useCases.headline: Who uses AudioProctor and how.
useCases.intro: AudioProctor is for any assessed student who needs audio or text support: students with reading disabilities, English Language Learners in applicable assessments, and students with IEPs or designations requiring an accommodation.
useCases.card1Body: A student has a designation requiring audio or text support during provincial assessments. The teacher uploads the official audio track, records their own read-aloud, or pastes the assessment text directly. The student uses the extension during the exam on their managed Chromebook: a locked player for audio, or a fullscreen reader with built-in read-aloud for text.
useCases.card2Body: Schools with only a few accommodation students don't need a full assistive tech platform. One teacher, one assessment (audio or text), one code. There's no provisioning, no student accounts, and no coordination with IT for each assessment.
useCases.card2BodyNote: Free tier covers it. No infrastructure required.
useCases.card3Title: IT deploys once, every school has it
useCases.card3Body: IT adds the AudioProctor extension to the Google Admin Console policy. Every managed Chromebook in the division gets it automatically on next sign-in. No teacher installation, no help desk tickets, no version mismatch across schools.
useCases.card3BodyNote: Division tier: IT deploys once, every school has it.
useCases.faqQ1: Does this work on any Chromebook?
useCases.faqA1: Yes. AudioProctor works on any Chromebook running Chrome OS. For managed devices, IT can force-install the extension through Google Admin Console so teachers don't need to do anything. Unmanaged Chromebooks can also install it manually from the Chrome Web Store (coming in a later release).
useCases.faqA2: No. Students never sign in. They enter a short access code, given verbally by the teacher, and the extension opens directly to the assessment. There is no student-facing login, no email required, and no account creation.
useCases.faqA3: Only the teacher who created the assessment. Audio files are stored in a private storage bucket; text assessments are stored in the database. Access is controlled by row-level security tied to the teacher's Google account. Even the access code doesn't reveal the content. It only works through our API, which verifies the code and returns only what's needed for the student's session.
useCases.faqQ4: What happens when the access code expires?
useCases.faqA4: Assessments and codes expire automatically after 7 days by default (the division tier allows custom expiry windows). When an assessment expires, the access code stops working and the content is deleted. Teachers can also delete assessments manually at any time from the dashboard.
useCases.faqQ5: What's the difference between audio and text assessments?
useCases.faqA5: Audio assessments play a locked fullscreen audio player. The student listens to the recording. Text assessments display the passage in a fullscreen reader with built-in read-aloud powered by the device's text-to-speech. Both use the same access code and exit word flow, and both are locked to the Chromebook until the teacher provides the exit word.
useCases.faqQ6: Is this compliant with privacy legislation?
useCases.faqA6: AudioProctor does not trigger a Privacy Impact Assessment under Alberta's Access to Information Act (ATIA). No student personal information is collected or stored at any point. Students are completely anonymous to the system. The only personal data processed is teacher email addresses, which are already covered by existing Google Workspace agreements at participating divisions.

about.label: About
about.headline: Built by someone in the room.
about.problemBody1: When a student requires audio or text accommodation during an assessment, the expectation is clear, but the tools rarely are. Teachers are expected to deliver audio support or provide a text-to-speech reader for students with IEPs or designations, and the standard assessment environment gives them almost nothing to do it with.
about.problemBody2: The workarounds are familiar: another adult in the room reading aloud, screen readers that weren't calibrated for assessment content, or aging playback hardware that may or may not still work. None of these are consistent. None of them scale. And none of them are what the accommodation is supposed to look like.
about.problemBody3: The friction is structural. Schools have moved to managed Chromebooks and browser-based assessment delivery, but accommodation tooling hasn't kept pace. The gap isn't theoretical. It shows up every time a teacher has to improvise a solution five minutes before a test begins.
about.solutionBody1: AudioProctor was built to fill that gap. A teacher uploads an audio file or pastes assessment text, generates a short access code, and hands it to the student. The student enters the code in a Chrome extension on their Chromebook. For audio, a locked fullscreen player opens. The student listens and replays as needed. For text, a fullscreen reader appears with built-in read-aloud powered by the device's text-to-speech. When the assessment is done, the teacher provides an exit word to close the session.
about.solutionBody2: No student accounts. No student data. No IT ticket per assessment. The extension is deployed once by IT through Google Admin Console and works across every Chromebook in the division from that point forward.
about.pricingBody: AudioProctor is priced by the scope of the purchase. A teacher can sign up free. A school can buy a plan from their minibudget. A division can sign one contract that covers every school, every teacher, and every Chromebook. The price scales with how much of the organization is covered, not with how many features are unlocked. {link}
about.builtByTitle: Built by someone in the room
about.builtByBody1: AudioProctor was built by an IT administrator at a real Alberta school division who ran into this problem and couldn't find a solution that didn't create new privacy risks or require significant infrastructure. The tool reflects what actually happens in schools: how assessments get run, how teachers operate under time pressure, and what IT departments will and won't support.

privacy.label: Privacy Policy
privacy.headline: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: AudioProctor is designed from the ground up to protect student privacy. We collect no student personal information and store no student data.
privacy.section1Body: We collect only the information necessary to operate the service: teacher email addresses (via Google OAuth), uploaded audio files and assessment text, and anonymous session events (access code entered, playback started, playback completed). No student names, IDs, device identifiers, or personal information is collected or stored.
privacy.section2Body: Teacher email addresses are used for authentication and account management. Audio files and assessment text are stored to deliver accommodation during assessments. Session events are used for anonymous usage analytics.
privacy.section3Body: Data is stored securely in Supabase, hosted in Canada. Assessments and access codes expire automatically after 7 days (or as configured by the division/customer). Deleted data is purged from backups within 30 days.
privacy.section4Body: We use Google OAuth for authentication, Supabase for database and storage, Vercel for hosting, and Stripe for payment processing. Each service processes only the data required for its function.
privacy.section5Body: For privacy questions or data requests, contact {email}.
